changed.title: Perfect matching in a 3 by 3 bipartite graph, on its 9 edge bits: some circuit of at most 11 AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in at most two computes it
changed.statement: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 9 (fun x : Fin 9 → Bool => (x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6)) 11
changed.unlocks: a lower rung of the ladder for 3 by 3 bipartite perfect matching
changed.context: FIND (beat this), one rung of a ladder at 13, 12 and 11. Your answer is an object: a gate list (AND, OR, NOT, at most two inputs each; wires 0 to 8 are the inputs) and its output wire; decide the equality over all 512 inputs. The best circuit known to us has 14 gates, replayed on every input; whether 11 is possible is unknown to us.

6: at most 11 gates in all, with exactly 1 NOT gate and 6 to 8 AND gates.
7: at most 11 gates in all, with exactly 1 NOT gate and 9 to 11 AND gates.

changed.sketch: A calibration of our constructions; no claim attached either way. Answer with a circuit, not an argument: a gate list (operation, wires read; wires 0..n-1 are the input bits in the statement's order, gate j writes wire n+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire. Judged by one kernel evaluation over every input. Any search method is welcome; only the circuit is checked. We hold 14 gates with no NOT gate: expand along the first row and share every 2 by 2 minor. Constructions only so far; our solver run at this size did not finish, so we do not know if this bound exists.

changed.unlocks: whether the second input of a lone OR reader always implies the OR of the vertex's two neighbours at the open shape
changed.context: Answer with a circuit (gate list and output wire), checked by evaluation on the 128 inputs. Ten gates is the least size for this function (checked), so any witness is a least circuit. What a found circuit shows: the other wire of the OR can be true where both neighbours are false, in a least circuit of a graph with no triangle; on two small graphs WITH a triangle we have such circuits (computed). Tried (computed): on the 5-cycle none; on the 6-cycle no least circuit has the shape; on the 7-cycle one 600 CPU s search gave no verdict. Truth unknown to us.

changed.title: An AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 26 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 14 vertices with 21 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. Proved by exhibiting ONE circuit with at most the stated number of gates of fan-in at most two that computes the edge function (true exactly when both ends of some edge are true) on every input; checked by evaluation. The best circuit known to us has one gate more (computed, not checked). Size: minutes if such a circuit exists. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
